  • Series
    Film
    Florence Gould Theater

    Jean-Luc Godard: Unmade and Abandoned

    Tuesday, September 15, 2026 - Thursday, October 15, 2026

    Over the course of his phenomenally productive career, Jean-Luc Godard had hundreds of unmade and abandoned projects. By setting a selection of Godard’s completed films in dialogue with others by him and a range of different directors, this program reveals the vast and varied phantom body of unrealized ventures that lie behind or in the intervals in his completed oeuvre and casts in relief his creative process.

    Family Saturdays – Fall ’26

    Saturday, September 19, 2026 - Saturday, December 5, 2026

    L’Alliance New York continues its Family Saturday series with multidisciplinary arts programming that engages young people and their families through visual art, storytelling, and Francophone cinema. The immersive program features visual arts workshops, story time in French, live theater performances, and film screenings.

  • Series
    Film
    Florence Gould Theater

    La Chienne

    Tuesday, September 29, 2026

    4:00 PM
    7:00 PM

    The principle of ‘remaking’ was central to Godard’s work. As he put it in relation to Breathless: ‘What I wanted was to take a conventional story and remake, but differently, everything the cinema had done.’ It is a concept he revisited almost six decades later in The Image Book, the opening section of which is titled simply ‘Remakes’. In the early 2000s, Godard expressed a desire to make a contemporary version of Jean Renoir’s La Chienne (1931), planning to cast Maurice Pialat in the role played by Michel Simon in the earlier adaptation.

    Florence Gould Theater

    J. Hoberman presents Moi, un noir

    Thursday, October 1, 2026

    6:30 PM

    Introduced and book signing of Across the Movi-Verse: Writing on Film, 2011–2021 with J. Hoberman

    To celebrate the publication of Across the Movi-verse, a brand-new anthology of J. Hoberman’s previously uncollected essays, tributes, reviews and ruminations from his post-Village Voice career, on subjects including the films of the Obama era, film maudit, Chantal Akerman, and Triumph of the Will, L’Alliance New York welcomes the legendary critic to present Jean Rouch’s seminal feature Moi, un noir, considered by Jean-Luc Godard to be “The greatest French film since the Liberation.”

  • Series
    Film
    Florence Gould Theater

    The Silence of the Sea with Hail, Sarajevo

    Tuesday, October 6, 2026

    4:00 PM
    7:00 PM

    In the late 1990s and 2000s, Godard had a series of unrealized projects with Claude Lanzmann, Bernard-Henri Lévy and Marcel Ophuls relating to the Holocaust, Jewishness and Palestine–Israel. He also had several related solo ventures, including a contemporary version of Vercors’ 1942 World War II novel Le Silence de la mer (The Silence of the Sea), which Jean-Pierre Melville had adapted as his first feature. In Godard’s planned film, to be called Le Silence de la terre (The Silence of the Earth), the action was to be transposed from occupied France to occupied Palestine. Although he abandoned this project, it informed his luminous 2004 Sarajevo-set feature Notre musique (Our Music). This program also includes the stunning short film that Godard made in 1993 in protest at the refusal of European governments to take action over the siege of Sarajevo, Je vous salue, Sarajevo (Hail Sarajevo, 1993).

  • Series
    Film
    Florence Gould Theater

    The Audiovisual Script: Passion and Zoetrope

    Friday, October 9, 2026

    6:30 PM

    This special screening explores Jean-Luc Godard’s groundbreaking approach to filmmaking through his innovative ‘audiovisual scripts’ – experimental video notebooks that replace the traditional written screenplay. Focusing on his acclaimed film Passion, the program spans work from 1981 to 2006, bringing together rare test footage, preparatory video scripts, the remarkable video essay he made afterwards, and the short film he eventually made from the test footage. This constellation of material offers a unique insight into how Godard developed ideas through audiovisual collages of image, text and sound, blending cinema, painting, and experimentation.

    Florence Gould Theater

    The Shameless Old Lady and La Chinoise

    Tuesday, October 13, 2026

    4:00 PM
    6:15 PM
    8:30 PM

    Contrary to what one might conclude based on how few plays Godard adapted as films, he was deeply interested in the theater and had numerous unrealized theatrical projects over his career. René Allio, whom Godard interviewed for Cahiers, ventured into filmmaking from theater, and his first feature La Vieille dame indigne (The Shameless Old Lady) is a beautifully observed, gently subversive adaptation of a Brecht short story, featuring Sylvie (real name Louise Pauline Mainguené) as a widow determined to enjoy her remaining years to the full. Godard’s wide-ranging exploration of theater in the 1960s culminated in La Chinoise (1967), a film that exemplifies his desire in this period to combine and blend theatrical and cinematic forms. ‘One should make theater in the cinema’, as he put it, ‘mix things up’.

    Florence Gould Theater

    Sauve la vie (qui peut): A Reconstruction

    Thursday, October 15, 2026

    6:30 PM

    A digital reconstruction by Michael Witt of a remarkable montage film created by Godard at the 1981 Rotterdam Film Festival from his film Sauve qui peut (la vie) and reels from four other films: Old and New (aka The General Line) by Sergei M. Eisenstein and Grigori Alexandrov (1929), Cops by Edward F. Cline and Buster Keaton (1922), La Terra Trema by Luchino Visconti (1948), and Man of Marble by Andrzej Wajda (1977). This montage film, which Godard titled Sauve la vie (qui peut), was screened just once and seen by only a handful of people. It constituted an extension of his wide-ranging experimentation with the juxtaposition of film reels during his exploratory lectures on cinema history in Montreal and Rotterdam in 1978 and 1980-1981, respectively, and anticipated his later videographic montage practice, which would culminate in Histoire(s) du cinéma.
